en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīyānuloma (4), Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (2) 20.5.
Mahantaraduka (The Great Pairs)
Dependent on a state with an object, a state with an object arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state without an object, a state without an object arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state without an object, states both with and without an object arise by way of root condition. ... [Three.]
Dependent on a state with various objects, a state without an object arises by way of root condition … three.

Dependent on a state that is neither with an object nor with various objects, a state with an object arises by way of root condition … three. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are nine; under object condition, three;
under predominance condition, five … pe … under mutuality condition, six … pe … under prenascence and repetition conditions, one … pe … under non-disappearance condition, nine.
Dependent on a mental state, a mental state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a non-mental state, a non-mental state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a non-mental state, both mental and non-mental states arise by way of root condition. … [Three.]

Dependent on a state that is not consciousness (*nacitta*) and a state that is not non-consciousness (*nanocitta*), a state that is not consciousness arises by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*) … one. (Abbreviated.
Under root condition there are five … pe … under non-disappearance condition there are five.
Dependent on a non-mental state, a mental state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a non-mental state, a non-mental state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a non-mental state, both mental and non-mental states arise by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of the root condition (*hetu*), there are nine; ... [and so on] ... in the case of the prenascence and repetition conditions (*purejāta*, *āsevana*), there are five; ... [and so on] ... in the case of the non-disappearance condition (*avigata*), there are nine.
Dependent on a state not associated with consciousness (*nacittasampayutta*), a state associated with consciousness (*cittasampayutta*) arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state not associated with consciousness, a state dissociated from consciousness (*cittavippayutta*) arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state not associated with consciousness, states both associated with consciousness and dissociated from consciousness arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state dissociated from consciousness, a state dissociated from consciousness arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state dissociated from consciousness, a state associated with consciousness arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state dissociated from consciousness, states both associated with consciousness and dissociated from consciousness arise by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state both non-associated with consciousness and non-dissociated from consciousness, a state associated with consciousness arises by way of root condition... three. (Abbreviated. Nine for root; three for object;
five for predominance... pe ... six for mutuality... pe ... one for prenascence and repetition... pe ... nine for non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state not associated with mind, a state associated with mind arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state not associated with mind, a state dissociated from mind arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state not associated with mind, states both associated with mind and dissociated from mind arise by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to the root condition (hetu), there are nine; with respect to the object condition (ārammaṇa), three; with respect to the predominance condition (adhipati), five ... pe ... with respect to the mutuality condition (aññamañña), six ... pe ... with respect to the prenascence and repetition conditions (purejāta-āsevana), one ... pe ... with respect to the non-disappearance condition (avigata), nine.
Dependent on a state not originated by mind (nacittasamutthāna), a state originated by mind (cittasamutthāna) arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state not originated by mind, a state not originated by mind arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state not originated by mind, there arise states both originated by mind and not originated by mind, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
Nine in the case of root; nine in the case of object; five in the case of predominance … pe … nine in the case of non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state not coexistent with consciousness, a state coexistent with consciousness arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state not coexistent with consciousness, a state not coexistent with consciousness arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state not coexistent with consciousness, states both coexistent with consciousness and not coexistent with consciousness arise by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of the root condition, there are nine; in the object condition, nine … pe … in the prenascence and repetition conditions, five … pe … in the non-disappearance condition, nine.
Dependent on a state that does not accompany consciousness, a state that accompanies consciousness arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that does not accompany consciousness, a state that does not accompany consciousness arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that does not follow the mind, states that both follow the mind and do not follow the mind arise by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. Nine in the case of root;
nine in the case of object ... pe ... five in the cases of prenascence and repetition ... pe ... nine in the case of non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state that is not conjoined with or originated by mind, there arises a state that is conjoined with and originated by mind, by way of the root condition.
(Abbreviated. Nine under root; nine under object ... pe ... five under prenascence and repetition ... pe ... nine under non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is not conjoined with or originated by mind and is co-existent, there arises a state that is conjoined with and originated by mind and is co-existent, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of the root condition, there are nine; in the object condition, nine ... pe ... in the prenascence and repetition conditions, five ... pe ... in the non-disappearance condition, nine.

Dependent on a state that is not conjoined with, originated by, or concomitant with consciousness, there arises a state that is conjoined with, originated by, and concomitant with consciousness, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. In the case of the root condition, there are nine;
in the object condition, nine ... pe ... in the prenascence and repetition conditions, five ... pe ... in the non-disappearance condition, nine.
Dependent on an internal state, an internal state arises by way of the root condition... three.
Dependent on an external state, an external state arises by way of the root condition... three.
Dependent on both an internal and an external state, an internal state arises by way of the root condition... three. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root condition, nine; in the case of object condition, five …pe… in the case of non-disappearance, nine.
Dependent on a state not derived from clinging (*anupādā*), a state derived from clinging (*upādā*) arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
In the case of root condition, five; in the case of object condition, three …pe… in the case of prenascence and repetition, one …pe… in the case of non-disappearance, five.
Dependent on a state not associated with clinging (*anupādinnadhamma*), a state not associated with clinging arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*). (Abbreviated.

There are five under the root condition, two under the object condition (*ārammaṇa*), one under the predominance condition (*adhipati*) … [and so on] … one under the repetition condition (*āsevana*) … [and so on] … five under the non-disappearance condition (*avigata*).
